summary:
I've written plan.md: a long, low single-storey house of white stucco and dark timber under a pale slab roof that rises only 1.5 blocks over a 10-cell half-span. Its eaves are 2 deep, beam ends stick out past them every 3 cells, and a flat carport roof sits one level lower beside it. The street side is blank apart from a tan ledgestone wall, a clerestory strip and an orange door; the back is floor-to-ceiling glass between dark posts, opening onto a kidney pool. Those layered horizontals, the central atrium and the teal-and-white car on the driveway are what make it read as an Eichler or Palm Springs house. Long white-stucco, dark-timber post-and-beam bungalow: stepped-slab near-flat gable on beam lines every 3, flat carport deck one level lower, blank street face with ledgestone wall and orange door, all-glass garden side, open-sky atrium at the centre.
Open-plan public core (gallery, galley kitchen, dining, living with sunken pit and freestanding fireplace) west of the atrium; corridor with 3 bedrooms and 2 baths east.
Teal/white car, desert front yard, kidney pool and patio behind. 6 parts; elements.md and the plan.md designer sections are written.

house shell and ground: parts/shell.mjs builds the house shell: pit floor y=0, entry reveals, smooth_stone base y=1, white stucco walls y=2..4 with every OPENINGS cell left as air (south glass wall and house corners left air for part 4), dark_oak_planks header y=5 skipping beam lines, interior partitions and doorways, spruce ceiling y=5, terrazzo/spruce/quartz floors at y=1 with pit, atrium and chimney left open.
make.sh finishes with a whole build.nbt: the shell line shows 670 placed, no REFUSED and no OFF-PALETTE; mcd check reports walkable end to end and no unsupported blocks, with 30 floating cells (ceiling and ring header) that the roof must support. Front-left and back elevation tiles show a low white box with dark header band and openings.
Ticked plan.md part 1 and elements 1 and 7; added Notes lines to plan.md on the air corners, the south body, the floating cells and the rectangle terrazzo.
polish: Elements 13 (slider gaps) and 16 (atrium ring) are only partly done: the shell leaves the air openings and the ring body, and part 4 must glaze y=4 and place the ring glass and posts.

Bedding y=-1 is not written: the grid has no y<0, and build.mjs drops and counts it. Dirt y=0 is already laid over the whole lot by build.mjs, so the shell does not restate it. The plan's dirt-y=0-under-house instruction is covered by that.
Part 4 must place posts at the four house corners (x=10/31, z=8/25, y=2..4), since the shell leaves them air. The south wall body y=2..4 is air for glazing. Both are noted in plan.md Notes.

Spruce ceiling y=5 (z=9..13, z=20..24) and the ring header at z=18 (x=17..18, 20..21) float until the roof slabs and beams at y=6 and y=5 arrive. The mcd check reports 30 floating cells; the roof part should clear this.

waste.what: Worked out every wall segment, partition doorway and window opening cell range by hand from OPENINGS and ROOMS (about 40 stucco_wall calls with y-ranges worked out per segment).
waste.cost: about 40 hand-computed boxes, several re-checks of door and corner cells against plan.md; roughly 4 minutes of the 12
waste.tool: A wall-with-openings helper: give a wall line, its base/body/header y-ranges and the opening list (x/z range, y range) from OPENINGS, and it fills the rest of the line. Or a plan-from-openings text grid through layers().

waste.what: Laid the public-room floor as 16 hand-cut terrazzo rectangles around the pit, atrium, chimney and bedroom cells, checked cell by cell for gaps.
waste.cost: 16 boxes plus a gap check; a missed cell at (20..21,1,20) was found only on re-reading
waste.tool: terrazzo_floor takes a box only. A predicate or mask form (fill a room box minus named reserved boxes) would replace the hand-cut list; ROOMS boxes could feed it directly.

waste.what: Reasoned about the door wall z=9 and corner ownership between shell and part 4 posts, which the plan states two ways.
waste.cost: several minutes of reading plan.md; resolved and recorded in plan Notes
waste.tool: A per-cell ownership table (which part writes each cell) generated from the spec, so conflicts are visible before writing.

summary:
site, carport and paving: Part 2 (site, carport, paving) is built in parts/site.mjs: sidewalk, driveway with joint rows, sand yard and side strips, gravel beds, stepping pads, entry landing, carport (deck, posts, beams, fascia, floor), breeze screen at z=21, patio, pool deck and lawns (dirt-only, pool cells left as air).
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt. The site part placed 933 blocks with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE writes. Checklist items 5, 6, 11, 18, 19, 25 are ticked in elements.md, and plan.md's checklist shows 2 site as done.
Rendered tiles (front-left, street) show the carport on the west with its deck, posts and checkerboard screen, and the driveway, sand and paving read where the plan puts them.
polish: elements.md item 24 (patio and pool deck) is only half done: the paving is in, but the loungers, patio table and palm (29,31) belong to parts/back.mjs. Item 24 is left unticked for that reason.
Breeze screen end cells (1,3,21) and (9,3,21) show as orphans in mcd check: they touch the build on one face only. They are the screen's own ends, so I left them; flagged in plan.md Notes.

Lawn and sand-strip precedence at x=0, z=22..25 (sand kept, lawn only over dirt) and at x=9, z=8..21 (carport floor wins) is my reading of plan.md's overlapping ranges; the back part should not overwrite it.

waste.what: Wrote a local ground-painting helper (lay) because the vocab helpers only write into air (so they can't lay paving over the bedding dirt) or return inconsistent shapes (a count in some, {placed, skipped} in others).
waste.cost: one helper written and debugged; about 15 rectangles worked out by hand for paving, sand, gravel and lawn
waste.tool: a vocab helper paint_box(g, [x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1], block, {over: [...], skipPool: true}) that overwrites named ground cover and returns one shape

waste.what: Resolved the overlaps by hand: lawn x=0..9 z=22..33 against the x=0 sand strip, the x=9 strip against the carport floor, and the driveway joints under the carport.
waste.cost: reasoning over plan.md's site table, no retries
waste.tool: a plan.md overlap table or a precedence order per cell (e.g. a per-cell owner list) for the ground layers

waste.what: Filtered `mcd check` output by eye to find my own orphans and floating cells; most of the floating list belongs to other parts (shell ceiling at y=5).
waste.cost: one check run read in full; about 30 flagged cells sorted by hand
waste.tool: mcd check --bbox <part box> or a per-part filter that lists only cells inside the part's own footprint

waste.what: Looked at tiles by eye for whether the carport and paving read correctly, no measured check.
waste.cost: two tile reads
waste.tool: a per-part render that crops to the part's footprint

summary:
roofs, beams and fireplace stack: parts/roofs.mjs builds the stepped slab roof (four bands, dark_oak_slab fascia and hole rims at the atrium and chimney), the eight beam lines at y=5 (z=5..28), the y=6 glass (gable ends x=10/31 and atrium ring x=16/22), and the fireplace stack at x=20..21 z=21..22 with the lit campfire.
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt. The roofs part placed 738 blocks with no REFUSED writes and no off-palette blocks; `mcd check` reports 0 floating and 0 unsupported blocks.
The render reads as a low dark-fringed slab roof with beam ends and the chimney stack; I checked the front, back and front-left views.
polish: Atrium ring posts and the rest of the ring glass (plan item 16) are part 4's; only the y=6 ring glass at x=16 and x=22, z=14..17, is placed here.
fascia_ring is not used: roof_band's fascia option gives the same dark_oak_slab rim per band half, and fascia_ring cannot split a z-run by band half.
`mcd check` reports 16 orphan beam ends (dark_oak_log at z=5 and z=28 on the eight beam lines). These are the intended exposed tails, held by the beams behind them, so I left them.

waste.what: Transcribed the four roof bands (eight z-runs with half and y) from plan.md's ROOFS table into roof_band calls by hand.
waste.cost: about 8 calls worked out by reading the table; no checking tool
waste.tool: a roof-from-band-table helper (or a band list in the plan's JSON) that takes z-runs, y, half and holes and emits roof_band calls

waste.what: Verified the roof, hole and glass placement by writing an ad-hoc node script that prints a block-letter map per layer (/tmp/peek-part3.mjs) because the toolkit has no per-layer or per-cell query.
waste.cost: one script and one run; the 'u'/'[' letter mapping was ambiguous and needed reading back
waste.tool: an `mcd layers build.nbt --y 6,7,8 --box x0,z0,x1,z1` command that prints per-layer letter maps with a legend

waste.what: Ticked the checklists in elements.md and plan.md with sed by hand.
waste.cost: one sed call, plus one retry after sed -i needed a '' argument on macOS
waste.tool: a `mcd tick <part>` command that ticks a part's checklist lines and elements items from the part's own file

summary:
facades, glazing and entry: parts/facades.mjs builds the south garden glass wall (posts on every beam line, glass bays, three slider glazings at y=4), the street face (clerestory, ledgestone feature wall with cap, orange acacia entry), the west and east windows with an open dark_oak utility door, and the atrium ring glass with posts.
make.sh gives a whole build.nbt: facades placed 218, refused 0, offPalette 0. Spot-checked cells match plan.md (door halves, slider gaps air at y=2..3 with glass at y=4, ring door gaps open, lintel post at (19,4,11)).
Gable-end glass at y=6 is written into air too; it floats until the roof band is in.
polish: Gable-end glass at y=6 (x=10 and x=31, z=14..19) floats in build.nbt until part 3 (roofs) lays the roof band; element 14 stays unticked because it is the roof's.
Atrium ring glass crossing band C at y=6 (x=16 and x=22, z=14..17) is the roof's and not placed by me.

Visual check was only the 300px elevation and street tiles, which are too small to judge the detail; the north face and the entry read correctly by position, but the stone, the clerestory and the glazing rhythm were not inspected at close range.

waste.what: Worked out every south-wall and ring coordinate by hand: the glass segments between beam lines and the slider gaps, the x=19 lintel posts, and the atrium door-top cells.
waste.cost: About 10 minutes of reasoning, no retries; the coordinates were correct on the first run.
waste.tool: A facade-band helper that takes a wall line, a beam-line rhythm and opening lists (slider, door, window) and emits glass or post segments, so each wall is one call.

waste.what: Read four vocab files and the build-library B helpers to learn each helper's signature and return shape. They differ across h1 to h4: some return a count, some {placed, skipped}, and h4 takes a writer. There is no utility_door helper, so I wrote one.
waste.cost: About 3 minutes of reading, plus one local helper.
waste.tool: A vocab index listing each helper's signature and return shape, and a utility_door / door-pair helper in vocab.

waste.what: Spot-checked about 30 cells one by one with a node script to confirm they match plan.md (air where the openings are, glass or posts where they should be).
waste.cost: One script run of about 30 lookups; no retries.
waste.tool: `mcd check` or `mcd cells build.nbt --at x,y,z ...` to read blocks at listed coordinates, and a per-part skipped-count (writes refused because the cell was occupied) in parts-report.json. runParts today reports only refused and off-palette, so air-only skips are invisible.

summary:
car and front garden: parts/front.mjs builds the parked two-tone 50s car (3,1, nose north), palms at (12,3) and (30,4), a cactus bed (two saguaros, three barrel cacti), three dead bushes on the sand, and the mailbox at (9,1). make.sh ran clean: 104 blocks placed, no refused writes, no off-palette blocks.</summary>
<parameter name="waste">[{"what":"Dead bush placement: wrote a local put() helper and chose three sand cells (14,7), (21,7), (27,7) by hand after reading plan.md's sand and gravel extents.","cost":"one edit, about 3 minutes of reading and coordinate checks","tool":"A vocab helper such as plant_scatter(g, cells, id) or a sand-cell list in plan.md's front-yard row would have made this a one-liner."},{"what":"Reading the vocab helper sources (palm, saguaro, barrel_cactus, car_50s, mailbox) to learn their signatures and whether they only write into air.","cost":"one grep and two sed reads of vocab/h1-h4.mjs","tool":"A generated vocab index (name, signature, cells written, air-only yes/no) in vocab/ or the toolkit's helper list would have saved the reads."},{"what":"Checking the render by eye for car, palms, cacti, mailbox placement; the dead bushes were not visible at that tile scale and were not checked individually.","cost":"two tile reads, no zoomed render","tool":"`$MCD render build.nbt --crop x0,z0,x1,z1` (a zoomed tile of one part's footprint) would make the by-eye check precise."}]
polish: Cactus bed cells at y=0 under the saguaros and barrel cacti are gravel (laid by part 2), but cactus needs sand beneath it; part 2 must lay sand on (26,0,3), (24,0,2), (28,0,2), (23,0,4), (29,0,4). Recorded in plan.md Notes. Locked cells, so not fixed here.
The dead bushes at (14,7), (21,7), (27,7) were placed but not confirmed in the render; check at merge.
mcd check flags 8 orphan jungle_leaves at palm crown tips (y=6). They are persistent leaves and harmless, but they will show as orphans until the roof part lands.
The floating spruce/dark-oak cells at y=5 near x=14..21 z=18..25 come from parts 1 and 4, not this part.

summary:
pool, patio and garden details: Back garden part built in parts/back.mjs: kidney pool (water at y=0, quartz coping lip at y=1 on the deck), 3 loungers and a patio table with parasol at z=26..28, palm at (29,31), 4 garden lamps (entry path at (17,5),(21,5); pool at (11,31),(24,32)), seeded short grass on the back lawns.
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt; this part wrote 234 blocks with 0 refused and 0 off-palette. Checklist and elements 23, 24, 26 ticked; plan Notes has a line on the coping and parasol choices.
Tiles rendered, but at 300px per view the furniture is too small to judge up close.
polish: Pool coping is at y=1 (a smooth_quartz slab lip on the deck cells beside the pool), not y=0 as elements.md item 23 says: the deck block at y=0 is part 2's smooth_stone, so the coping cannot sit there. Part 2 needs to leave those deck cells as they are.
Pool depth: build.mjs drops y<0, so the saved pool is one water layer at y=0 over air, with no liner or floor. The check does not flag it, but it reads as shallow water, not a basin.

Parasol: plan.md's patio_table helper says no parasol, but the parts spec asks for one. I built one (fence pole at y=3 on the table top, 3x3 quartz canopy at y=4); the pole sits on a half-slab, so it may read as floating at close range.
Entry lanterns from the parts spec were not built: only the four garden_lamp posts. Hanging lanterns at the door belong to the facade/entry part unless the orchestrator wants them here.

Close-range look not verified: the front-right and back-elevation tiles are too small to judge the loungers, table and coping. The part-2 paving and the other parts were still stubs, so the pool sits against bare dirt in this test build.
Palm crown leaves show as orphans in check.mjs (persistent jungle_leaves, expected for a palm; not a defect).

waste.what: Worked out the kidney pool coping cells by hand: the deck cells 4-adjacent to each pool row, and which of them the patio furniture and lamps could collide with.
waste.cost: about 4 minutes of reasoning and one rebuild; the coping had to go at y=1 because the deck is already smooth_stone at y=0
waste.tool: A helper that lists the deck or rim cells adjacent to a reserved footprint, and says which layer is free (the site part's paving sits at y=0, so the coping layer is the next one up). The kidney_pool helper could take a coping layer argument.

waste.what: Checked the lamp and lounger positions against the patio, deck and lawn boxes cell by cell in my head, with no tool to test a candidate position for collisions before writing it.
waste.cost: 2 rebuilds with make.sh (about 20s each) to move the lamps from z=4 to z=5 to match elements.md
waste.tool: A dry-run mode for parts (print the cells a helper would place and what they collide with, without writing) would have caught the z=4 vs z=5 lamp mismatch first time.

waste.what: Looked at the render tiles to judge the pool and furniture, but the 300px elevation tiles are too small to see detail.
waste.cost: 2 image reads that did not settle whether the loungers and parasol read correctly
waste.tool: A zoomed-crop render option (mcd render with a box argument, e.g. --box x0,z0,x1,z1 --zoom 4) so a worker can LOOK at its own footprint.

summary:
room: gallery: Gallery (room-1.mjs) built as an entrance hall: birch_slab bench at (17..18,2,10) with a hung lantern at (18,4,10) over it, drawn with layers() in one call. make.sh ran clean (room: gallery placed 3, no refusals or off-palette); room check says walk OK (6/6 reachable) and light min 9, 0 dark.
The box is one cell deep (z=10), so the gallery is a 7-cell walking line; the north-wall art and coat-hook wall did not fit. Plan.md Notes records this.
polish: Coat-hook wall and north-wall art: the box has no wall cells (item frames are entities, not blocks), so these need the box widened or the wall handed to part 1.
Furnishing is minimal: the one-deep box leaves only a bench and one hung lantern; no extra focal piece beyond the bench and lantern.
elements.md item 30 (entry gallery with a bench and a coat-hook wall) is only partly built, so it is not ticked. plan.md Notes records this.

waste.what: Worked out the gallery's walkable line and the lantern/bench cells by hand from the plan grid, then drew them into layers() rows.
waste.cost: about 3 layer rows and 2 retries of reasoning about which cells must stay clear for the path
waste.tool: A room-spec command that reports the one-deep walking line (cells every route must cross) and which cells are free to furnish, before drawing.

waste.what: Checked the hung_lantern helper's behaviour by reading vocab/h1.mjs: it silently places nothing when no block sits above, which is always true in a local build before the shell and beams are merged.
waste.cost: one grep and one reasoning step; I drew the lantern with B.lantern(true) through layers() instead
waste.tool: Helpers should report a skipped placement (or take a flag to place without the anchor check) so a local build does not drop furniture without warning.

summary:
room: kitchen: Kitchen part built in parts/room-2.mjs: galley along z=9 (iron fridge, quartz counter with smoker, cauldron and furnace, spruce upper cabinets), breakfast bar on z=12 with birch-slab stools on z=13, orange carpet mat at the hob.
Three hung lanterns at y=4 (11,10), (13,10), (11,12) light it: walk 18/18 reachable, light min 8, 0 dark cells, no refused or off-palette writes; make.sh produced a whole build.nbt.
The render reads as a kitchen (counters, bar with stools, cabinets); plan.md's room checklist has no line for it, so only elements.md item 29 is ticked.
polish: Stools are birch_slab bottom (galley_kitchen helper's choice), so they read as low benches rather than stair seats; acceptable but a stair-seat variant would match the spec's 'stairs as seats' better.
The 30 floating blocks reported by mcd check are spruce/dark-oak ceiling and header cells from other parts (roof not built yet), none in the kitchen box.

waste.what: Worked out counter, appliance and bar heights by reasoning about the block/slab stacking (full quartz counter at y=2, appliances at y=3, bar fence plus slab), which the galley helper already encodes.
waste.cost: about 3 minutes of reasoning and one wrong-height consideration
waste.tool: plan.md VOCABULARY should say which helper covers the galley and its heights, so a designer calls galley_kitchen directly without re-deriving stacking

waste.what: Placed lanterns by trial: first build had one dim cell (min light 7), I added the lantern the room check suggested and rebuilt.
waste.cost: one extra make.sh run and one check
waste.tool: a light-plan helper (e.g. hung_lantern spots chosen by the check's suggestion built in) or a planner that places lanterns to clear the dark cells before the first build

summary: room: dining: ["Dining (parts/room-3.mjs): sideboard on the west wall under the window (dining_set-style birch/spruce), spruce-top table for six with birch stairs as chairs (2 north, 2 south, 1 west, 1 east), and a hanging lantern at (13,4,16) over the table.", "make.sh produced a whole build.nbt; room dining reports 24 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette. Room check: WALK ok (23/23 reachable), LIGHT min 9, 0 dark cells; the render reads as a table with six chairs and a sideboard.", "Ticked elements.md item 28; plan.md Notes records that the pendant needs part 3's beam on x=13 and that the spruce panelling is not built (walls are shell-locked)."]
polish: Spruce panelling is not built in the dining room: the walls and ceiling are shell-locked, and the dining box has no free wall face to panel without cutting into the walking floor.
The pendant lantern at (13,4,16) hangs from the part-3 beam on x=13 (y=5). In this copy the beam is absent, so the check reports it unsupported; it should be supported once the roofs part is merged.
The terrazzo floor is laid by the shell part, not by this part.

waste.what: Worked out by hand that the table had to move from x=12 to x=13 so the west chair did not collide with the sideboard at (11,2,16), and checked the walk path cell by cell.
waste.cost: one re-run of make.sh and the room check; about 2 minutes of reasoning
waste.tool: A footprint-collision check in dining_set/sideboard (or a dry-run that reports overlapping furniture cells before placing) would have caught the chair/sideboard clash at write time.

waste.what: Re-derived the lantern placement rule because dining_set only places its lantern when the beam above exists, and that beam is part 3's, so my copy showed the lantern as unsupported.
waste.cost: one extra check run and a hand-written g.set fallback
waste.tool: A helper that says which cells a part depends on from earlier parts (e.g. a beam above a hung lantern), or a copy that includes the roofs part so pendants can be checked in isolation.

waste.what: Used sed -i with a single quoted expression on macOS, which failed because BSD sed takes the next argument as a backup suffix; I then used the Edit tool.
waste.cost: one failed command
waste.tool: No toolkit fix needed; this is a shell note: on macOS use the Edit tool or sed -i ''.

summary: room: living: ["Living room (parts/room-4.mjs) built into air only: sunken conversation pit (conversation_pit), two orange sofas (sofa_low), egg chair facing the atrium, birch sideboard with potted cactus, spruce-fence floor lamp with end rod, and seven hung lanterns.", "Verified: `room` reports WALK ok (53 of 53 floor cells reachable), LIGHT min 8 with 0 dark and 0 dim cells; the rooms render (from above and inside) reads as a pit with sofas and egg chair. make.sh gives 'room: living:48' with no refused or off-palette writes.", "Fireplace is part 3's (roofs stub in this copy), so the focal piece is not in this copy's build; the ceiling spruce_planks at y=5 float until the roof part lays y=6 slabs (check flags them)."]
polish: Freestanding fireplace is not mine (roofs part, x=20..21 z=21..22): the focal piece is absent in this copy's build until merge; the light check was run without the campfire.

Tulip side table (elements item 34) not built; no rugs or carpets on the floor; no panelling on the x=22 partition (it is white_concrete from the shell, so panelling would need a wall-panel helper over it or the shell to leave it).
`check` flags the living-room hung lanterns and spruce ceiling at y=5 as floating; they rest on the roof part's y=6 slabs, which are not in this copy.

waste.what: Worked out the walk and light answer by hand: which furniture cells block the 2-high path, whether a pocket (e.g. x=11 column behind the west sofa) is cut off, and where the egg chair back and side trapdoors land, from the helper source
waste.cost: about 3 planning passes, 1 real rebuild to fix the east-corner light (min 5 with dim cells), and a second rebuild to confirm (min 8, 0 dim)
waste.tool: A `room` dry-run that takes a furniture list (helper name + x,z + facing) and prints the walk and light result before any make.sh, so layouts are checked without a rebuild

waste.what: Looked up each vocab helper's footprint and facing convention by reading vocab/h1-h4.mjs (egg_chair back is on the facing side, sofa_low arms, sideboard trapdoor orientation)
waste.cost: about 6 file reads and several minutes of the 12-minute budget
waste.tool: A short footprint index in plan.md or the vocab README (helper -> cells it writes, facing meaning per helper)

waste.what: Hand-picked hung_lantern positions by checking the beam lines and ceiling rows (x=13,16,19,22 beams; z=20..24 ceiling; z=19 open), since hung_lantern silently returns 0 with no block above
waste.cost: 4 lantern spots tried, 2 extra spots added after the first light check
waste.tool: A helper that lists the valid hang cells for a room (cells with a block above) so lantern placement is chosen from that list

summary:
room: atrium: room: atrium (parts/room-5.mjs) is built: a jungle sapling tree as the focal piece on the west, a smooth_stone path between the two door pairs at x=19..20, a quartz stair bench facing the tree, large ferns, short grass, potted cacti.
Two hanging lanterns at (19,4,13) and (19,4,16) light the room; check gives WALK ok (29/29 reachable), LIGHT min 9, 0 dark.
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt; the atrium part placed 45 blocks with 0 refused and 0 off-palette.
polish: The lanterns at (19,4,13) and (19,4,16) hang from the beam at x=19, y=5, which is the roofs part's beam_line. `mcd check` reports them unsupported until that part is merged; no action needed from me once it is.

grass_block cannot be placed: the dirt at y=0 is locked by the shell, so the grass patch is short_grass and large_fern on y=1. If the shell should have laid grass_block in the atrium, that is a shell change, not mine.
The room reads sparse from above; the grass patch is small. Acceptable for this pass, not revisited after the one LOOK.

waste.what: Worked out each furniture cell by hand as a character grid and re-derived the x/z offsets for the tree, ferns, bench and two-high plants.
waste.cost: about 6 minutes of reasoning and 2 build runs to get the grid right
waste.tool: `mcd plan` could print a per-cell legend template (char key per floor cell, pre-filled 'free' vs 'wall' with the beam lines and door cells marked) so the furniture grid is drawn on a ready-made sheet.

waste.what: Looked up the stair facing convention, the layers() legend format ([block, state] pairs), and the two-high plant half states by reading build.mjs and vocab source.
waste.cost: 3 file reads and 1 failed guess at the legend format before the first build
waste.tool: A short build-library reference (one line per helper: B.stairs facing = back side, large_fern half=lower/upper, lantern hanging, persistent leaves) or a `mcd states <block>` that prints the valid properties.

waste.what: Checked by eye whether the lanterns and the tree sat under the right beams and light levels, after a separate `mcd check` run.
waste.cost: 2 extra commands
waste.tool: `mcd room` could report lantern support (beam present or not) and the focal-piece light level in the same run.

summary:
room: corridor: Corridor (room-6) built: x=23 walkway kept clear, spruce sideboard run with plant on the x=24 side (z=11..14), focal plant niche with two standing lanterns and a spruce panel backdrop (z=16..18), spruce panel at z=20, three hung lanterns under the ceiling planks.
make.sh whole build.nbt, room-6 placed 25 with 0 refused and 0 off-palette; room check OK (18/18 floor cells reachable, min light 12, 0 dark); render tiles done.
Item frames left out (entities, not blocks); the art is the spruce backdrop. Room view only from above (no inside view produced).
polish: No item-frame art: item frames are entities, so the focal is the plant niche and spruce panel backdrop at z=16..18.

waste.tool: A room-designer helper that prints, for a room box, which floor cells are walkway, which are doorway approaches, which ceiling cells can take a hung lantern, and which air cells above furniture are unreachable before drawing, so the grid is right on the first pass.

summary:
room: bedroom 1: Bedroom 1 furnished in parts/room-7.mjs: cyan bed with spruce headboard against the north wall, birch-slab nightstand, spruce wardrobe down the east wall, end_rod floor lamp, cyan rug, and three hanging lanterns (one over the bed head). 25 blocks, no refused or off-palette writes; make.sh produced a whole build.nbt.
Scratch check with the missing floor laid: walk OK (10 of 11 floor cells reachable; the 11th is the air cell on top of the headboard), light min 11 with no dark cells.
Not verified in the real build: the shell's bedroom floor is missing (see left), so the real room check fails at the floor level.
polish: Shell bug (parts/shell.mjs floors()): the bedroom and bath floor fills are called with 3 args, so y=1 under bedroom 1, bedroom 2, master, bath 1 and bath 2 is air. Fix: fill(g, [26,1,9], [30,1,12], "spruce_planks") and the same for the other four. Noted in plan.md Notes. Until fixed, the room walk check reads the floor at y=3 and reports NEEDS WORK. I verified on a scratch copy with the floor laid.

Structural check flags the lantern at (28,4,10) as unsupported because the beam_line at x=28 y=5 is not built in this copy (roofs part is a stub). The carpets at y=2 are flagged because the floor is missing. Both should clear at merge.
Not done: the 'from inside' view. I rendered from above only (scratch copy with the floor laid).
The air cell at (28,3,9), on top of the 1-high headboard, is counted unreachable by the walk check. It is enclosed and harmless, and the verdict is still OK.
elements.md item 31 covers three bedrooms; only bedroom 1 is built here, so I left the item unticked. The plan.md checklist lists only parts 1-6, so I did not tick it.

waste.what: Worked out the bed, nightstand, wardrobe and lantern cells by hand from the room grid, then retried after finding bed_double's footprint would block the door and window lane
waste.cost: about 3 rounds of cell-by-cell reasoning and two rebuilds
waste.tool: A room-furnishing helper that takes a room box and a furniture list (bed, nightstand, wardrobe, lamp) and checks lanes, door clearance and light before placing anything

waste.what: Built a scratch copy with the bedroom floor laid to see the walk and light verdicts, because the shell floor is missing in this copy
waste.cost: 2 extra save/load/check cycles

waste.cost: 3 tool calls

summary:
room: bath 1: Bath 1 (parts/room-8.mjs) built in its 2x3 box: cauldron tub with a sea_lantern plinth at the north end, a white_carpet mat in the middle row (the only standing cells, reached from the door), and a smooth_quartz_stairs WC plus cauldron basin with a glass_pane mirror at the south end. ./make.sh runs whole, 7 blocks placed, no refusals or off-palette.
With a scratch copy that adds the missing bath floor, `mcd room` reads OK: 6/6 floor cells reachable, minimum light 10, none dark.
The real build.nbt still reads NEEDS WORK because the shell's bath floor never lands (see left).
polish: Shell bug (parts/shell.mjs lines 143-146, not my module): fill(g, [26,1,14,27,1,16], "smooth_quartz") passes the 6-cell box as one argument, so the bath 1 and bath 2 floors (and the spruce bedroom floors on the same lines) are never written. Bath 1's y=1 floor is air in build.nbt, so `mcd room` reads the floor at y=3 and reports NEEDS WORK, and the sea_lantern and mat show as unsupported. Fix: fill(g, [26,1,14], [27,1,16], ...) etc.
Checked on a scratch copy with the bath floor added: the room is OK (walk 6/6, light min 10). Re-run the room check once the shell floor lands.

Elements item 32 (two bathrooms) is NOT ticked: only bath 1 is built here; bath 2 is part 9. bath_fit (vocab/h2.mjs) was not used: its slab lip at the mat row would block the door's 2-high path in a 2x3 room, so bath 1 uses its own layout. Worth a note in vocab for the 2-wide case.

The room is 6 floor cells, so the picture at room.png (scratch copy, rendered from above) is hard to read. The tub is one cauldron, not a two-cell tub. The sea lantern is on the floor, because a lantern can't hang: there is no ceiling over z=14..19.
plan.md checklist not ticked: it only lists parts 1-6 and has no room rows.

waste.what: Worked out the bath-1 floor grid by hand, then the furniture cells, the walk path and the light by reading the nbt with a throwaway node script (/tmp/peek14/peek.mjs) to dump a box region by y-layer.
waste.cost: about 4 tool calls, 2 full make.sh rebuilds, one scratch floor-injected copy to test the room check
waste.tool: mcd dump <nbt> --box x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1 (print blocks by y-layer). Would have shown the empty bath floor at once.

waste.what: Diagnosed the NEEDS WORK verdict by hand: the room check reads floor y=3 because the shell's bath floor is missing, not because the furniture is wrong. The shell bug (a 6-element array passed as one argument to fill()) was found only by reading shell.mjs.
waste.cost: about 3 tool calls and a standalone shell run
waste.tool: mcd check should flag a room whose box has no floor under it (y0-1 not solid) and a fill() call signature mismatch in a part. A per-part 'expected surfaces present' check would have caught this at make time.

waste.what: Compared the bath_fit helper's layout against the 2-wide room by hand. Its slab lip at the mat row blocks the 2-high path from the door, so I redrew the layout myself.
waste.cost: one read of vocab/h2.mjs plus a layout rethink, no rebuild wasted
waste.tool: A vocab helper with a walk-aware variant for 2x3 rooms, or an mcd room-fit command that tries layouts and keeps the one whose walk verdict is OK.

summary:
room: bath 2: Bath 2 en-suite (parts/room-9.mjs): quartz WC stair on the north wall, cauldron basin with a glass mirror, shower tray and iron-trapdoor head in the far corner, white carpet mat, two hung lanterns. Drawn as three y-layers with layers(): 8 blocks placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette.
Room check on the built nbt says UNREACHABLE because the shell never lays the bath floor at y=1 (see left). With that floor patched in a scratch copy, the walk is OK and every floor cell is lit at 12 or more.
polish: Shell bug (parts/shell.mjs floors(), not my module): the bedroom, bath and master floor fills use fill(g, [x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1], name), but fill takes two corners, so nothing is placed. Bath 2's y=1 floor (29..30, z14..16) is air in build.nbt, so `mcd room` reports UNREACHABLE and `mcd check` flags the carpet at 29,2,15 as unsupported. Fix in shell.mjs: pass the two corners as separate arguments. Noted in plan.md Notes.
room.png was rendered from a scratch copy with the floor patched (/tmp/room9-check), not from build.nbt; the real build's bath floor is blank until the shell is fixed.
Elements 32 (two bathrooms, bath 1 is another part) and 35 (lit, all rooms) span other parts, so I did not tick them. plan.md's part checklist has no room rows, so nothing to tick there.

waste.what: Checked which blocks sit at each height of the bath cells by writing a one-off node script that loads the nbt and prints blockAt per cell, to find why the floor was missing.
waste.cost: 1 script, 2 calls
waste.tool: mcd room should print the blocks under the box at y=1 when the floor is missing (it reported floor y=3 with no explanation), or mcd check should flag a box with no floor under it.

waste.what: Checked the palette ids one at a time because `mcd blocks --check` only reported the first id when given several.
waste.cost: 12 separate shell calls
waste.tool: mcd blocks --check should take and report every id in one call.

waste.what: Verified the walk and light by copying build.nbt, patching the missing y=1 floor, and saving to a scratch file, because the real build has the shell bug.
waste.cost: 1 node call plus 2 mcd room calls
waste.tool: mcd room --assume-floor or a per-room lint that names the shell's missing floor cells would have shown the cause straight away.

waste.what: Worked out stair facing and carpet/slab placement by hand from the build library, since the stair semantics were not clear from the docs.
waste.cost: 2 reads of the helpers
waste.tool: A stairs/slab state note in the palette or `mcd states stairs` would cut the guesswork.

summary:
room: bedroom 2: Bedroom 2 furnished in parts/room-10.mjs, inside its box only: wardrobe on the north wall, yellow rug, yellow bed head-south at x=30 with a barrel nightstand and standing lantern, lectern workstation with a spruce-stair seat, hung lantern over the bed foot, potted cactus on the wardrobe top.
make.sh runs whole (bedroom 2: 13 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette). Light at the feet is 10 to 14 with no dark cells; the walk check passes once the bedroom floor exists (see left).
Verified on a temp copy only, with the y=1 floor laid by hand; the room check and a from-above render were run on that copy, and no inside view was rendered.

So `mcd room build.nbt --only "bedroom 2"` reads NEEDS WORK (WALK UNREACHABLE, floor y=3). The floor is outside my box (y starts at 2), so I did not place it; the shell part needs to fill the bedroom floors at y=1 (also check bedroom 1, master and the corridor).

elements.md item 31 (corridor to three bedrooms) is shared with bedroom 1 and the master bedroom; only the bedroom 2 part is built, so I left it unticked. plan.md's checklist has no room entries, so nothing was ticked there.

The room tool reported 'unreached: 27,4,18' on the temp copy, a cell on top of the wardrobe. It is not a real floor cell (the ceiling at y=5 blocks it), so it looks like a tool counting quirk. Not verified further.
Only one look was taken: from above on the temp copy. No inside-view render was made, and the full-house tiles do not show the room because the roof covers it.

waste.what: Worked out each furniture cell's x,z,y by hand from the plan's floor grid and the layers() legend, then fixed the bed head/foot and the nightstand positions after one walk check showed a blocked door cell.

summary: inspection: Fixed the cross-part breaks in the mid-century house: the shell's bedroom and bath floors were never laid (a bad fill() call), and three hung lanterns hung over the open vault. Look pass was done at 300px elevations and the room sheet only; the car, the pool and the bath 1 layout (sparse, sea lantern plinth and tub) were not checked closely enough to call them right.
parts/shell.mjs fill() calls are the only broken helper calls I found; other parts were not audited for the same argument mistake.

waste.tool: a check that flags a floor/box fill whose floor layer is air, or a helper that rejects a 6-number array passed as a corner pair (fill() silently accepted it)

waste.tool: a light-placement suggester: `mcd light --suggest` listing candidate air cells (standable, free above, sand/lawn/paving) that would clear each dark cell
